dataset_name: Dots and SlipAgent Python code-search pilot
ranking: exact cosine; no HNSW approximation or distance cutoff
timings: Informational warm timings, not a controlled performance benchmark

queries.query: Reuse the locally downloaded encoder files before contacting the model hosting service.
Ignore padding when averaging token representations and scale the resulting vector to unit length.
Fingerprint the actual model weights and tokenizer so incompatible embeddings cannot share an index.
Keep inference from consuming every processor core on the machine.
Save source records and the nearest-neighbor graph atomically, keeping the previous version if publication fails.
Notice when another process has published a new search graph and reload the cached copy.
Reject embeddings with the wrong size, infinite values, or zero magnitude before storing them.
Find approximate cosine neighbors, then fetch only their matching source excerpts by identifier.
Keep the configuration and source data consistent while another writer updates the database.
Skip rereading and re-embedding a file whose timestamp and byte count have not changed.
Avoid recomputing embeddings when a file was touched but its contents stayed identical.
Remove previously indexed source files that have disappeared from the workspace.
Abort an update when a source file changes during the read.
Refuse a semantic query when the database was built using a different encoder.
Prevent recursive traversal from descending into dependency folders and build artifacts.
Preserve a few lines of context between adjacent source excerpts.
Emit complete search excerpts as machine-readable JSON rather than shortening the displayed text.
Inspect stored index metadata without initializing the embedding model.
Resolve a supplied filename against the project root and reject paths outside the allowed area.
Permit access to temporary files while retaining the project boundary for other paths.
Check whether a path belongs to the project independently of unrestricted access mode.
Skip file symlinks whose targets escape the permitted directories during traversal.
Finish resource cleanup even if the task waiting for it is cancelled.
Cancel and drain owned background work before running cleanup callbacks in reverse order.
Make simultaneous close requests wait on the same retained teardown task.
Discover repository guidance from several editor-specific rule folders and load it in sorted order.
Block an edit when applicable repository guidance has changed since it was shown to the model.
Remember exactly which instruction snapshot was included in a model request.
Detect an agent cycling through the same tool results and stop after recovery guidance did not help.
Exclude changing command log identifiers when deciding whether tool output is unchanged.
Detect sustained repeated prose in a streamed response while ignoring fenced source code.
Match a multiline edit target regardless of whether the file uses Unix or Windows line endings.
Refuse replacement edits that overlap in the original file.
Show nearby actual source when a requested replacement target cannot be found.
Stop retaining additional command output at the session quota without splitting a UTF-8 character.
Read a tail page of a saved command stream and return byte offsets for subsequent requests.
Make completed command output durable before closing its file handle.
Try native clipboard utilities appropriate to the desktop environment.
Encode copied text into a terminal clipboard escape sequence without accepting raw escape data.
